topic: The Hidden Revenue Leaks Costing Fitness Clubs

facts.label: Story
facts.value: The Hidden Revenue Leaks Costing Fitness Clubs

facts.label: Outlet
facts.value: Athletech News

facts.label: Article
facts.value: From failed payments to disconnected systems and processing costs, small gaps in the revenue cycle can add up quickly Failed payments alone can represent roughly 8% of a fitness club’s monthly revenue. For a club billing $600,000 a month, that puts $48,000 potentially at risk. And failed payments are only one place revenue can leak. Account freezes may not reach billing, cards expire without being updated, upgrades can miss the next draft and declines can sit untouched when alerts don’t reach the right person. For operators using multiple systems across membership, billing and payments, those leaks can add up fast. “Operators rarely lose money inside a system; they lose it in the handoffs between systems,” said Matt Popinski, chief customer and payments officer at Daxko. “Each platform may work fine on its own, but a member status, a card update, or a cancellation has to travel from one to the next, and every handoff is a chance for it to arrive late, arrive wrong, or never arrive at all.” Some of the resulting losses are easy to spot, but others are nearly impossible to trace. Chargebacks can be difficult to defend when the necessary information lives in another system, and in some cases, Popinski said, memberships have even been terminated over an expired card rather than a member’s decision to leave. There is also the time spent figuring out what went wrong.

topic: Fitness On Demand Adds 99 Mvmnt Workouts to Expand Digital Programming

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Fitness On Demand Adds 99 Mvmnt Workouts to Expand Digital Programming

facts.label: Outlet
facts.value: Health & Fitness Association

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Partnership brings expert-led strength, cardio, and wellness content to operators across Fitness On Demand’s in-facility, mobile and connected touchpoints MINNEAPOLIS, OCTOBER 14th 2026. Fitness On Demand, the commercial omnichannel fitness platform trusted by studios, gyms and wellness operators worldwide has announced a new content partnership with Mvmnt, a digital fitness platform known for expert-led coaching. The collaboration adds 99 Mvmnt workouts to Fitness On Demand’s existing library of more than 1,800 workouts, giving operators more ways to keep their programming fresh without adding equipment, headcount, or a separate app. Mvmnt’s content spans strength and bodyweight training, HIIT, boxing, dance and cardio, alongside yoga, Pilates, mobility and meditation, with sessions built around different life stages and fitness levels. That programming will be available across in-facility screens, workout spaces and mobile touchpoints, via Fitness On Demand, helping operators reach members both in-club and beyond the four walls. The additional content solves a familiar problem. Members expect variety, but building it in-house means more instructors, more scheduling and more cost. Incorporating Mvmnt’s library into Fitness On Demand’s existing platform lets facilities broaden their offering immediately, using the infrastructure they already have.

topic: The Boutique Cycling Industry Is Evolving and Local Ownership Will Lead the Next Chapter

facts.label: Story
facts.value: The Boutique Cycling Industry Is Evolving and Local Ownership Will Lead the Next Chapter

facts.label: Outlet
facts.value: Club Solutions

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Kara Willis, the president of CycleBar, explains why sustainable boutique fitness growth will increasingly rely on both strong studio economics and strong community connections. Boutique fitness has never been a static industry. Consumer preferences change, new workout formats emerge and the concepts that dominate one decade often look very different in the next. Indoor cycling is no exception. Over the past several years, we’ve watched the boutique cycling category experience tremendous growth, increased competition and a period of consolidation. Some established operators have pulled back or exited markets altogether, leading to questions about the future of dedicated cycling studios. But I don’t believe indoor cycling is going anywhere. Cycling ranked as the fourth most-booked workout category globally on ClassPass , with reservations increasing 6% year over year. I believe we’re entering a new chapter, one where successful operators understand their communities, run disciplined businesses and recognize that today’s fitness consumer expects more than a great workout. The Shift From Expansion to Sustainable Unit Economics I’ve spent much of my career in boutique fitness, working with brands including Orangetheory Fitness , F45 Training and TITLE Boxing Club before recently becoming the president of CycleBar.

topic: Athlone fitness studio raises over €1,000 in support of Breast Cancer Awareness

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Athlone fitness studio raises over €1,000 in support of Breast Cancer Awareness

facts.label: Outlet
facts.value: Westmeath Independent

facts.label: Deal
facts.value: raise €1,000

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Athlone fitness studio ØRA Wellness has raised over €1,000 in support of Breast Cancer Awareness with its Pink Wellness Morning. Run by local woman Aishling "Ash" Croughan, ØRA Wellness Studio is located on Athlone's Castlemaine Street. It has a range of fitness and wellness offerings, from yoga, dance and pilates, to breathwork and meditation. The Pink Wellness Morning was organised alongside life coach Libby Hayes, and brought together a group of women for a morning of gentle movement, breathwork, coffee, cake and connection, all in support of Breast Cancer Awareness. "The morning was a wonderful success, with such a positive atmosphere," Libby said. "It was fantastic to see everyone come together to support the cause, and I’m delighted that we’ve been able to make a meaningful contribution while enjoying a lovely morning together." Abbey and Aisling extended their thanks to everyone who attended and donated, and to the local businesses who supported the event including Mary’s SuperValu Athlone, A Room in Bloom, and Sláinte Coffee Shop.

topic: Unravel Health Raises €2.5M for At-Home Hormone Testing

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Unravel Health Raises €2.5M for At-Home Hormone Testing

facts.label: Outlet
facts.value: Fitt Insider

facts.label: Deal
facts.value: raise €2.5M

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Special measures. What’s happening: The women’s hormone monitoring company secured €2.5M to launch the Micro Lab, an at-home diagnostic device. Vantage point. Using saliva-reading biosensors, Unravel’s device—shipping in 2027—checks estradiol and other biomarkers in minutes, surfacing daily symptom patterns isolated blood tests can miss while building a longitudinal picture of whole-body health across life stages. Turning the home into a personal lab, new funds will allow it to add additional hormones and expand into men’s health. Mixed signals. Noninvasive hormone tracking is already entering mainstream wellness. But, from Oura and Fitbit to Clair Health and Lume Health , algorithmic estimates from wearable tech have come under scrutiny. Opting to make gold-standard testing more DIY, Unravel will join Eli Health in instant salivary tech, while Oova and Mira scale daily urine tests and Level Zero and Adaptyx retool CGMs. Punchline: From snapshots to signals, Unravel is bringing lab-grade precision and near-instantaneous insight to a category still shaped by fragments, not the full story.
